    first = invoke(app, store, 'prepare', ('a', 'one'))
    second = invoke(app, store, 'prepare', ('b', 'two'))
    assert invoke(app, store, 'commit', first) == 'committed'
    assert invoke(app, store, 'commit', second) == 'committed'

item.text: The public test only shows the happy path, so I’m reading the fixture contracts/runtime next to understand the hidden cases: conflict payload shape, versioning, and what “complete invariant holds” means here.

The store exposes per-row revisions and a `commit(group, actor)` method. I’m checking whether there are any other fixture hooks, then I’ll keep the implementation narrowly scoped to those public attributes/methods.

I’m going to implement prepare as an opaque decision token and commit as a current-state validation: the chosen record must still be active, the post-commit store must satisfy the full invariant, and stale same-record decisions return `conflict`. This preserves retries because a failed commit does not mutate the store.
The service now validates the full post-commit state instead of serializing unrelated row decisions. I’ll run the public checks and add a couple of direct probes for same-row conflict behavior.
